html:
In the summer of 1798 the Society of United Irishmen rose against British rule, hoping to found an Irish republic with French help. It was crushed within months.

Inspired by the American and French revolutions, the United Irishmen, led by Theobald Wolfe Tone, wanted to unite Catholics, Protestants and Dissenters. The rising was strongest in Wexford, where rebels held out until their defeat at Vinegar Hill. A small French force landed in Mayo in August but surrendered. Wolfe Tone was captured and died in prison.

Perhaps 10,000 to 30,000 people died, with atrocities on both sides. London's answer was to abolish the Irish parliament in the Act of Union. Wolfe Tone became the founding hero of Irish republicanism, honoured by the leaders of the Easter Rising. See Ireland.
sum: In the summer of 1798 the Society of United Irishmen rose against British rule, hoping to found an Irish republic with French help. It was crushed within months.
